targetAudience.primary: Architects designing governed agent decision and tool-execution systems
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands model confidence, abstention, tool calls and policy gates.
targetAudience.readerProblem: Professional-looking evidence can increase a model's willingness to act without increasing what is knowable.

whyNow: A same-day primary-research preprint reports large commitment shifts under evidence presentation, causal fabricated-panel evidence, knowability-first mitigation and response-format fragility across a heterogeneous model roster.

externalHook.description: Presentation form changes action commitment even when informative content and stated belief barely change.

coreProposition: Epistemic evidence should feed an independently inspectable action-qualification predicate: professional presentation and the model's generated commitment must not become execution authority when the underlying question remains unresolved, and the gate must be tested across presentation and output-format changes.

originalValue.description: Translates the reported epistemic/action separation into an external execution qualification boundary with presentation and format invariance tests.

readerTakeaway: Ask whether evidence can resolve the question before considering confidence or action text; make execution depend on an external predicate, not the model's self-selected commitment.

supported: The preprint reports commitment rising from 6.5% to 54.0% across evidence escalation.
Fabricated and real panels are statistically equivalent in the reported comparison.
Knowability-first and one fine-tuning intervention reduce commitment, while rigid formats can remove protection.
unsupported: Equivalence between ANSWER choice and real irreversible tool effects
uncertain: Which resolvability predicate transfers to deployment
Whether the effect replicates under real tool consequences

firstPartyRole.rationale: The conclusion is an independent action-qualification research finding.

decisionReason: The experiment supports a causal presentation/content distinction and a bounded architecture interpretation while preserving heterogeneity and validity threats.
